text: My name is Koh Tze Rui
I'm a Year 3 Computer Engineering student at NUS
I always knew I wanted to be an engineer.
I was naturally drawn to hard problems,
chasing the intellectual high of figuring things out.
So I did what every aspiring engineer does—I tried everything.
Software engineering. Containerisation. Abstraction.
Then quant. Algorithm books. Chasing the money. 💸
But after two years of grinding through national service and into university...
I just got really bored.
By Year 1, I'd quietly stepped away from engineering. 😶
Then one day, a friend sent me a link.
An HPC competition. Build a single board computer cluster.
I thought—why not?
And the rest was history. 🚀
Turns out, what I needed wasn't a different field.
It was a harder problem.
Grinding through the night to chase the last bit of performance in the system.
That's the kind of challenge that keeps me alive. 🔥
I think my slightly competitive personality helped a bit.
(okay... maybe more than a bit)
Sometimes you don't find your path by walking forward. You find it by getting bored enough to look sideways.
Every dead end taught me something. Every detour shaped what I was actually looking for.
Keep chasing the problem that won't let you sleep.
I used to think engineers were the ones who built the most.
Now I think they're the ones who refuse to stop until it's right.
